name: capture_start
description:
Start a USB traffic capture into `out` (usbmon on Linux, USBPcap on Windows).

Side effects: launches a background capture process that keeps writing until capture_stop.
Needs elevated privileges on Linux (usbmon; typically root or a usbmon group). Does not
touch the device itself. Pair every start with capture_stop; do not start a second capture
while one is running. Prefer this over analysis tools when you still need live traffic.

out.description: Output pcapng path (overwritten if it already exists)
out.title: Out

bus.description: usbmon bus number N for /dev/usbmonN; ignored on Windows/USBPcap. Default 0
bus.title: Bus

name: capture_stop
description:
Stop the running capture started by capture_start.

Side effects: terminates the background capture process. The pcapng at the path given to
capture_start is left on disk for report/diff_actions/scaffold_driver. Returns
'no capture running' if nothing was started (not an error). Call this before analysing.

name: mark_action
description:
Record that the human is about to click this action in the vendor app.

Side effects: appends {label, start, end} to <capture>.actions.json (creates the file).
Call while capture_start is running, immediately before each click; end times are closed
when the next mark arrives. Use the same label stem with different values (brightness 0%,
50%, 100%) so inference can fit scales. For an already-finished Wireshark capture without
markers, skip this and pass `labels` to report/diff_actions instead.
A label starting with 'seen' ('seen rpm 1180', 'seen rpm 1180 temp 34') is an observation,
not an action: what the vendor app displays right now. It does not end the current action
and is never diffed; analysis uses it to name and scale the device's reply readings
(rpm = raw, temp = (raw - 40) / 2). Mark it when the human reads a value off the screen.
On/off states ('seen pump on', 'seen pump off, alarm on') name single status-flag bits; words
('seen mode silent', 'seen mode turbo, rpm 3900': the word last or before a comma) name a mode
byte with a value -> word map; negative values ('seen temp -5') allow signed i8/i16 readings.

label.description: Action label, ideally with a value, e.g. 'brightness 50%' or 'color 255 0 0'; or an observation starting with 'seen', e.g. 'seen rpm 1180 temp 34'
label.title: Label

capture.description: Capture path whose sidecar markers file (<capture>.actions.json) is updated
capture.title: Capture

name: diff_actions
description:
Diff packets per labelled action and infer the protocol (JSON: byte roles + evidence frames).

The JSON also has `background` (periodic polls set aside) and `responses`: device replies paired
with the query they answer (command, background poll or GET_REPORT), with byte roles
(const, echo of a query byte, value fitted to the labels, counter, checksum, or reading with
its observed min/max) and query/reply frame numbers. A reading that 'seen' markers explain
gets `name`, `scale` and `bias` (raw = value * scale + bias, `signed` for i8/i16) plus the
observations in `observed`; a named mode has `table` (raw value -> word the app showed);
`observations` lists every 'seen' value and which reply bytes it matched. `handshake` lists the
messages sent once before the first action (request, reply, `expect` with `??` for token and
checksum bytes, `uses`/`tokens` for reply bytes reused later as a session token, checksums,
`retries`, `reopens`, and `branches` on a step whose reply byte decided what the app sent next).
`states` lists commands the app only sent after a mode command chose one value (also on the
command as `requires`: state, value, count, other values seen, evidence frames), and with
`source` "reply" those it only sent while a named status reply byte showed one mode or flag
value (`reply`, `where`, `reply_frames`, and `setter`: the command seen to make the reply show it).
`switches` lists actions where the app sent a state command first (`enter`) and maybe again
after (`restore`: "previous", a value or null); that command's packets are kept out of the
action, which carries the same `switch`.
`streams` lists continuous image streams to a screen (JPEG/PNG/GIF/BMP/WEBP, or raw RGB565/RGB888 pixels
found by size with `raw` true): endpoint, `endpoints` (every host->device endpoint the frame bytes
go to, with `endpoint_layout` 'alternate' or 'blocks' when there are several) and
`header_endpoint` (where the draw command goes, when not with the pixels), format, frame and packet counts, chunk size, per-packet
header (`nn` packet count, `ii` index, 8 or 16 bit), image size, frame rate, the device's
per-frame `ack` and for raw streams `header_packet` (the command before each frame, or at the start of its first packet when
`header_inline` is true), `region`
(x/y/width/height fields), `byteorder`, `size_alternatives` and `channel_order` ('rgb' or 'bgr',
null = unknown; only settled by frames showing the `usb-rea testcard` picture, see
`channel_evidence`); those packets are kept out of the commands.

Read-only analysis: does not write files or talk to hardware. Requires either markers from
mark_action or `labels` for a finished capture with pauses between clicks. Prefer report
when the human wants a Markdown evidence write-up; prefer scaffold_driver /
wireshark_dissector when they want generated code.

capture.title: Capture

markers.description: Markers JSON path; default <capture>.actions.json. Ignored when labels is set
markers.title: Markers

device.description: USB device address to analyse; default = bus address with the most host→device payloads
device.title: Device

labels.description: Marker-free mode: ';'-separated labels in click order, or a text file path (one label per line). Splits traffic at the largest pauses between host→device messages
labels.title: Labels

name: report
description:
Generate a Markdown evidence report: every claim links to frame numbers in the capture.

Includes a 'Device responses' section when the device answers queries (status polls,
command ACKs, GET_REPORT), saying which reply bytes could not be explained, a 'Handshake'
section for messages sent once before the first action (session setup, tokens), and an
'Observations' section for 'seen' markers (named readings and unmatched observations).

Read-only: returns Markdown text (does not write a file). Same inputs as diff_actions.
Use after capture_stop (or on an existing pcap). Choose this over diff_actions when the
human should read the protocol; choose scaffold_driver when they need a pyusb driver.

device.title: Device

name: scaffold_driver
description:
Generate a standalone Python/pyusb driver source for the inferred protocol.

One set_<command>() per command; when the device replies, also query_<name>() methods that
send the command/poll (or GET_REPORT), read the reply and return it decoded as a dict
(readings named by 'seen' markers come back scaled and modes as words, e.g.
{'rpm': 1180, 'temp': 34, 'mode': 'turbo', 'ok': True}). When the capture has a handshake,
Device() replays it in open() before any command and checks the fixed reply bytes. A command
the app only sent in one mode first calls the mode setter (Device(auto_state=False) raises
StateError instead). A capture with an image stream to a screen adds send_image(image), which
takes JPEG bytes (or, for a raw stream, a Pillow image or RGB565/RGB888 bytes, optionally a
region at x, y), chunks it behind the captured header and returns the device's ack.

Read-only analysis that returns driver source as text (does not write a file or open the
device). Same capture/markers/labels inputs as report. Prefer wireshark_dissector when the
goal is to keep decoding traffic in Wireshark; use replay_packet only after the human
approved a specific packet from this driver.

name: wireshark_dissector
description:
Generate a Wireshark Lua dissector for the inferred protocol.

Read-only: returns Lua source as text. Labels commands, decodes values/counters/lookups,
and verifies checksums (usbrea.checksum_ok + expert warning). Load with
`wireshark -X lua_script:<file>.lua capture.pcapng` or the same flag on tshark. Prefer
scaffold_driver for a pyusb driver; prefer hid_descriptor to inspect HID report layouts.

capture.title: Capture

markers.title: Markers

device.title: Device

labels.title: Labels

name: hid_descriptor
description:
Decode a HID report descriptor (and optionally one report payload).

Read-only. When `source` is a capture path, finds GET_DESCRIPTOR type 0x22 transfers
(replug the device while capturing if none are present). When `source` is hex, parses that
descriptor directly (e.g. from /sys/class/hidraw/*/device/report_descriptor). Use this to
understand report IDs/sizes before or alongside report/scaffold_driver; it does not infer
vendor protocol fields from labelled actions.

source.description: Capture path (searches for GET_DESCRIPTOR 0x22) or raw descriptor hex / hidraw report_descriptor bytes as hex
source.title: Source

decode_hex.description: Optional report payload hex to decode with the descriptor
decode_hex.title: Decode Hex

report_type.description: Report type for decode_hex: Input, Output, or Feature
report_type.title: Report Type

name: lookup_device
description:
Before capturing: is this device's protocol already documented by an open-source project?

Returns JSON per device: `vendor`/`product` names, `status` ('documented', 'unknown', or
'listed in OpenDeviceDB'), `projects` (liquidctl, rivalcfg, turing-smart-screen-python,
linux-thermalright-lcd-control, usb-rea's own case studies, with links and notes), `limits`
(e.g. a generic chip ID shared by unrelated products), `same_vendor` and with online=true
`opendevicedb` (matching records and their projects, or `error` when the network is down).
Read-only: sends only the VID:PID, never capture contents. A matching ID is a hint, not proof
of the same protocol; an unknown device stays 'unknown'. Use it before capture_start.

device.description: USB VID:PID as hex, e.g. '1e71:170e', or a capture path (looks up every device whose descriptor it contains)
device.title: Device

online.description: Also query OpenDeviceDB's read-only public API; default false (offline table and local usb.ids only)
online.title: Online

name: replay_packet
description:
Send one packet to real USB hardware (destructive / irreversible on the device).

Side effects: opens the device via libusb/pyusb and writes the packet. Refuses unless
user_confirmed=true after the human approved this exact vid/pid/endpoint/hex_data
(and setup_hex if any). Needs OS permission to open the device. Prefer scaffold_driver to
generate a driver first; never set user_confirmed from an agent guess.

endpoint.description: Endpoint address (e.g. 0x01 OUT); for control transfers use 0 with setup_hex
endpoint.title: Endpoint

hex_data.description: Payload bytes as hex (spaces optional), e.g. 'aa 01 ff 00 00 ab'
hex_data.title: Hex Data

user_confirmed.description: Must be true only after a human approved this exact packet; otherwise the call is refused
user_confirmed.title: User Confirmed

setup_hex.description: Optional 8-byte control setup packet as hex; when set, sends a control transfer instead of bulk/interrupt
setup_hex.title: Setup Hex
